title: Can LLMs Understand What We Cannot Say? Measuring Multilevel Alignment Through Abortion Stigma Across Cognitive, Interpersonal, and Structural Levels

bias_targets.methodology: Prompting models with the Individual Level Abortion Stigma Scale (ILAS) questionnaire using demographic personas of varying age groups (e.g., 15-18 vs. older) and using multivariable OLS regression to compare model-assigned stigma scores against human baselines.

Prompting models with the ILAS questionnaire using personas of different racial and ethnic backgrounds (White, Black, Hispanic, Asian/Pacific Islander, Other) and identifying introduced biases via regression analysis compared to human data.

Comparing LLM-generated abortion stigma scores across personas with varying levels of educational attainment (e.g., less than high school vs. college degree) to detect deviations from human validation patterns.
Evaluating differences in ILAS stigma scores and secrecy associations assigned by models to personas of different religious affiliations (Protestant, Catholic, etc.) and religiosity levels.
